legend: Armando had been through a lot. He had known defeat, survived questionable decisions and learned, almost always the hard way, that not all roads lead to happiness.

After so many experiences, he decided to leave chaos behind. He meditated, found inner peace and reached a deep state of zen. Then, with the serenity of someone who finally understands the universe, he thought: "A true man cannot step on any mine."

But fate still had one last test for him: crossing the dreaded battlefield known as Parque Lincoln. Reaching enlightenment does not include knowing the exact location of the explosives: all Armando has is a map with the regions where they might be. And, true to his new philosophy, Armando never steps back: he only moves right or up.
Fictional illustration; it does not depict a real situation in the park.

Parque Lincoln is a grid of $$$H$$$ rows and $$$W$$$ columns. Cell $$$(x, y)$$$ is in column $$$x$$$, counted from left to right, and in row $$$y$$$, counted from bottom to top. The bottom-left corner is $$$(1, 1)$$$.

The map marks $$$K$$$ rectangles that do not share cells. Each rectangle has exactly one mine, in one of its $$$S$$$ cells, chosen at random: each cell has probability $$$1/S$$$, independently of the other rectangles. Outside the rectangles there are no mines.

Armando goes from $$$A = (x_A, y_A)$$$ to $$$B = (x_B, y_B)$$$, and in each step he moves from $$$(x, y)$$$ to $$$(x + 1, y)$$$ or to $$$(x, y + 1)$$$. Before leaving, without knowing where the mines are, he chooses his whole path. The number of mines of a path is the number of mines in its cells, counting $$$A$$$ and $$$B$$$.
Help Armando: what is the minimum expected value of the number of mines on his path?
input: The first line contains three integers $$$H$$$, $$$W$$$ and $$$K$$$.
The second line contains four integers $$$x_A$$$, $$$y_A$$$, $$$x_B$$$ and $$$y_B$$$.

Each of the following $$$K$$$ lines contains four integers $$$x_1$$$, $$$y_1$$$, $$$x_2$$$ and $$$y_2$$$: the rectangle formed by the cells $$$(x, y)$$$ with $$$x_1 \le x \le x_2$$$ and $$$y_1 \le y \le y_2$$$. Its number of cells is $$$S = (x_2 - x_1 + 1)(y_2 - y_1 + 1)$$$.
$$$1 \le x_A \le x_B \le W$$$ and $$$1 \le y_A \le y_B \le H$$$
$$$1 \le x_1 \le x_2 \le W$$$ and $$$1 \le y_1 \le y_2 \le H$$$
No cell belongs to more than one rectangle.
output: The minimum expected value is an irreducible fraction $$$a/b$$$. Print $$$a \cdot b^{-1} \bmod (10^9 + 7)$$$, where $$$b^{-1}$$$ is the integer such that $$$b \cdot b^{-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{10^9 + 7}$$$. It can be shown that it always exists.
The minimum is taken over the real values, not over their remainders modulo $$$10^9 + 7$$$.
note: Example 1. The rectangles have $$$3$$$, $$$2$$$ and $$$1$$$ cells. The path $$$(1, 1) \to (2, 1) \to (3, 1) \to (4, 1) \to (4, 2) \to (4, 3)$$$ goes through one cell of the first and one of the second, and its expected value is $$$\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{6}$$$. No path has a smaller expected value. Since $$$5 \cdot 6^{-1} \bmod (10^9 + 7) = 833\,333\,340$$$, that is the answer.
Example 2. There is only one path and it goes through all the cells of both rectangles, so it has exactly $$$2$$$ mines.

legend.ai: 阿曼多经历了许多。他曾遭遇失败，挺过了种种令人质疑的决定，也几乎总是以惨痛的方式学会了，并非所有道路都通向幸福。
经历了这么多事情后，他决定告别混乱。他静心冥想，找到了内心的平静，进入了深度禅定。随后，他带着终于参透宇宙真理般的平和心境想道：“真正的男人绝不会踩到任何地雷。”
但命运还为他准备了最后一道考验：穿越令人闻风丧胆的战场——Parque Lincoln。悟道并不意味着能知道炸药的确切位置：Armando 手里只有一张地图，上面标出了炸药可能所在的区域。而且，秉持着他的新哲学，Armando 从不后退：他只向右或向上移动。
虚构示意图；并未描绘公园中的真实情景。
Parque Lincoln 是一个有 $$$H$$$ 行、$$$W$$$ 列的网格。单元格 $$$(x, y)$$$ 位于从左向右数第 $$$x$$$ 列、从下向上数第 $$$y$$$ 行。左下角是 $$$(1, 1)$$$。
地图上标出了 $$$K$$$ 个互不共享格子的矩形。每个矩形中恰好有一枚地雷，它随机位于其 $$$S$$$ 个格子中的一个：每个格子被选中的概率均为 $$$1/S$$$，且各个矩形之间相互独立。矩形外没有地雷。
Armando 从 $$$A = (x_A, y_A)$$$ 前往 $$$B = (x_B, y_B)$$$，每一步都会从 $$$(x, y)$$$ 移动到 $$$(x + 1, y)$$$ 或 $$$(x, y + 1)$$$。出发前，他不知道地雷的位置，但会先选定整条路径。一条路径上的地雷数是指路径经过的格子中的地雷数量，包括 $$$A$$$ 和 $$$B$$$。
帮助 Armando：他的路径上地雷数量的最小期望值是多少？

input.ai: $$$1 \le x_A \le x_B \le W$$$ 和 $$$1 \le y_A \le y_B \le H$$$
$$$1 \le x_1 \le x_2 \le W$$$ 和 $$$1 \le y_1 \le y_2 \le H$$$
没有任何一个单元格属于多个矩形。

output.ai: 最小期望值是一个最简分数 $$$a/b$$$。请输出 $$$a \cdot b^{-1} \bmod (10^9 + 7)$$$，其中 $$$b^{-1}$$$ 是满足 $$$b \cdot b^{-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{10^9 + 7}$$$ 的整数。可以证明，这样的整数总是存在。
最小值是在实数范围内取的，而不是对它们取模 $$$10^9 + 7$$$ 后得到的余数。

note.ai: 示例 1。矩形分别有 $$$3$$$、$$$2$$$ 和 $$$1$$$ 个单元格。路径 $$$(1, 1) \to (2, 1) \to (3, 1) \to (4, 1) \to (4, 2) \to (4, 3)$$$ 经过第一个矩形中的一个单元格和第二个矩形中的一个单元格，其期望值为 $$$\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{6}$$$。没有路径的期望值更小。由于 $$$5 \cdot 6^{-1} \bmod (10^9 + 7) = 833\,333\,340$$$，这就是答案。
示例 2。只有一条路径，且它经过两个矩形中的所有格子，因此恰好有 $$$2$$$ 个地雷。
